This is a short, simple reschedule note, so I'll follow the simpler message shape (the style guide allows a simpler structure when the audience doesn't need the full one). No tools used beyond the guidance reads above — no file created, no Outlook opened, no send.

## Draft Text

**To:** [RECIPIENT NAME/EMAIL — to be confirmed]
**Subject:** Demo rescheduled: Tuesday → Thursday

[GREETING — e.g., "Hi [Name],"]

The demo originally scheduled for **Tuesday, [ORIGINAL DATE]** has moved to **Thursday, [NEW DATE]**. [Optional: same time/location, or note if time/location also changed — TBD.]

**What changed:**
- **Date:** Tuesday [ORIGINAL DATE] → Thursday [NEW DATE]
- **Time:** [UNCHANGED / NEW TIME — to be confirmed]
- **Location/link:** [UNCHANGED / NEW LINK — to be confirmed]

Please let me know if this new time doesn't work and I'll find an alternative.

[Optional closing line, e.g., "Looking forward to it."]

---

## Must be confirmed before this could be sent

1. **Recipient(s)** — name/email address(es) are unknown; placeholder only.
2. **Exact original date** (the Tuesday being replaced).
3. **Exact new date** (the Thursday being moved to).
4. **Time** — whether it stays the same or changes.
5. **Location/meeting link** — whether it stays the same or changes.
6. **Sender's greeting/tone preference** and whether a send (not just a draft) is authorized.

This is text only — no file was created, no EML generated, and no Outlook draft was opened.
